original_question: Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group self-dual?
target_in_paper: Problem 37 in Section 2 ("Problems of 2025"): "Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group self-dual?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target essentially verbatim. It identifies the exact lattice class in Problem 37—lattices isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of a group—and asks the same self-duality question.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should define "self-dual": if a lattice L belongs to the class, must its dual lattice L^op also belong to the same class?

The quantifiers should be explicit: for every lattice L that is isomorphic to a sublattice of N(G) for some group G, ask whether there exists some group H such that L^op is isomorphic to a sublattice of N(H).
It helps to specify that N(G) denotes the lattice of normal subgroups of G ordered by inclusion.
The paper does not impose finiteness or other extra hypotheses here, so a stand-alone version should avoid accidentally adding such restrictions.
refined_question: Let C be the class of lattices L for which there exists a group G such that L is isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice N(G) of normal subgroups of G, ordered by inclusion. Is C self-dual; that is, whenever L belongs to C, must the dual lattice L^op also belong to C?
